Blue Arena is what happens when Blue Archive fans decide the official game’s combat isn’t quite enough—and build their own full multiplayer shooter around the students instead.
Instead of the original game’s top-down auto-battles, Blue Arena drops you into real-time matches where you personally control a Blue Archive character. You pick a student, equip whatever guns you want, and jump into team fights that mix first-person and third-person shooting. Every student has their own unique active skill, so the matches become a mix of gun skill and ability timing. Mobility is high, fights tend to be quick and aggressive, and there’s a clear sense of counterplay between different kits.
You can queue into public matches, set up private games with friends, or fight against AI. There’s also a PvE survival mode that leans into wave-based or zombie-style gameplay, sometimes set on maps inspired by familiar Blue Archive locations like Abydos. The PC version is the real one; a mobile build exists, but the community generally treats it as a stripped-down side option rather than the proper experience.
The whole project is the work of a Chinese developer known as 125690d. It’s still early in development (versions like 0.0.1 and 0.0.3 have appeared), with new maps, logos, skills, and features rolling out over time. Distribution and updates mostly happen through Chinese QQ groups and shared download links, while gameplay clips circulate on YouTube and Bilibili. Because it’s a pure fan creation, it has no official connection to Nexon or Yostar.
It’s easy to mix this up with the official game’s own PvP mode (called Tactical Competition, Arena, or Tactical Challenge depending on the server). That official mode is fully automated—your team fights another team without any real-time control. Blue Arena is the opposite: you are the one aiming, moving, and activating skills.
In short, Blue Arena is the fan community’s answer to the question “What if we could actually play as the students in a proper competitive shooter?” It’s rough around the edges in the way early fan projects often are, but it delivers exactly that fantasy—Blue Archive characters, real guns, real player skill—in a package that the original game never attempted
